newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan says committed to settlement with Uganda.
newsitem.headline: Sudan says committed to settlement with Uganda.

text.p: Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir was quoted on Saturday as saying his country will abide by an Iranian-mediated settlement with Uganda.
The official Sudan news agency (SUNA) said Bashir made the statement during a meeting with the Iranian deputy foreign minister for Arab and Islamic affairs, Hussein Shah Islam.

Under a September 9 agreement, mediated by Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, Sudan and Uganda agreed to work to halt rebel activity in the border area. They accuse each other of supporting rebel groups.

But tension renewed after Uganda's Minister of State for Defence Amama Mbabazi said two Sudanese MiG planes last weekend dropped bombs at army barracks in the northwestern town of Moyo, 16 km (10 miles) south of Sudan's border, but missed their target.
Iran's deputy foreign minister visited Uganda at the start of his tour to try and resolve the latest crisis and make the agreement work.
He said Uganda is also committed to the agreement. Uganda will send a team to a tripartite meeting, expected to be held on Monday.
Bashir said a Sudanese delegation would also attend the Tehran meeting.
The Iranian Minister said there is a good chance that his country's mediation to reconcile Sudan and Uganda would succeed if the United States did not apply any pressure. He did not elaborate.
"The (Iranian) initative will succeed if America lifts its hands and does not practise pressure," Islam said.
